arms.better: TM did find and edit the right implementation, but its run spent most of its budget revisiting the same completion and flag-parsing paths and repeatedly probing Go installation/GOROOT details; the event-derived usage reports 4.1M input tokens and 63 tool calls. It reached the 64-step limit after an internal submission error and printed `something went wrong` plus a retry command, without a concise summary of completed work or verification, so a user could not tell whether to trust the partial patch or whether retrying would repeat the investigation. Earlier setup output also needed correction because `tm events` requires a subcommand and macOS has no `timeout` binary. The merged test-file checkout followed by `go test ./...` passed mechanically, but the TM ticket itself ended failed.

OpenCode stated a short plan, located the exact append operation quickly, made an isolated-slice fix with a regression test, ran `go test ./...`, and clearly reported the result. The independently applied PR test file and second full-suite run also passed. The added regression test checked backing-array safety with an `Execute` setup but did not reproduce the precise `os.Args`/ValidArgsFunction case from the issue; using the upstream regression test itself would make the implementation test more directly representative.
